headline: Brent settles at $109.86 and Strategy drops about 10% on MSCI's new rules; BTC ETFs bleed another $82.4M on 10/16 and weighted funding falls back from 9.81% to 3.80% as the weekend goes quiet.
summary: Pressure from oil and tech stocks carried into Friday: ETFs swung back to provisional outflows and the Coinbase premium stayed negative, so US spot demand is still weak. The leverage that rushed back the day before was more than halved, and price is consolidating around 81K on thin volume. The market stage stays bull (day 9) and the exit framework is neither triggered nor close; next, watch Monday's ETF prints, the Strait of Hormuz and the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

cycle.lead: Market stage: bull (since 2026-10-09, day 9); 38 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA (threshold 30).
points: 200-day MA 72,425, above 70,338 thirty days ago and still rising; capitulation already seen (2026-06-30, 58,525).

Evidence lights 3/6 (strength of evidence only, not part of the call): MVRV above its 1-year mean (1.514 vs 1.435), realized cap +1.3% over 30 days, close above the short-term holder cost basis 74,443 (10/11) are lit; 12-month momentum (−24.6%), 90-day exchange supply (+0.95%), and STH cost vs True Market Mean (−6.11%, 10/11) are not.

Readings: extrapolating the last 30 days linearly, STH cost crosses above the True Market Mean around 12/15 (prior estimate 12/10); assuming flat price, 12-month momentum turns positive around 2027-01-31. Both are assumptions, not forecasts.
By rule, falling back to bear requires 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; days below now: 0. Tidemark low test: no break of 58,525 before 12/19.

news.title: At least 12 ships attacked around the Strait of Hormuz in a week and one container ship sunk, with both the US and Iran claiming control; Brent touched $110 intraday and settled at $109.86 (+3.7% on the day, +4.9% on the week), WTI at $101.41, Brent's highest close since May
news.read: Higher oil keeps inflation and hike expectations alive; the site's 10-year yield of 5.10% and real yield of 2.78% remain elevated, a macro headwind for risk-asset valuations. BTC only slipped on thin volume. This is price and funding backdrop: it does not change the market stage or touch the 200-day MA (−11.0%) or any exit condition.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs saw about $82.4M of net outflows on 10/16 (SoSoValue $82.39M, Trader T $82.41M): IBIT −$71.8M, FBTC −$10.61M, the rest flat; Trader T puts October-to-date at −$614.9M
news.read: The two sources are within 2%, so the site lists 10/16 as a provisional value. After 10/15 was confirmed at only +$5.1M, flows turned negative again; the seven complete days 10/07–10/15 total −$856.1M. Together with a −0.138% Coinbase premium, US spot demand remains the weakest link. Realized cap is still +1.3% over 30 days; weak flows, not a framework condition.

news.title: After MSCI finalized its non-operating-company rules, Strategy (MSTR) fell about 10% intraday Friday to $135.16, a market cap of about $57.2B, down about 12% on the week
news.read: A falling share price narrows Strategy's room to fund BTC buys with stock and preferred issuance, another sign of slowing demand outside ETFs. JPMorgan's $2.8B passive-selling estimate is about selling shares, not BTC, and the two-period rule lowers the odds of an immediate removal. BTC was roughly flat; the site has no direct gauge for this, so it is medium-term institutional backdrop.

news.title: CME FedWatch shows the odds of a hold at the Oct 27–28 FOMC rising to about 85% (about 72% a day earlier); Fed Chair Warsh gave no new rate signal
news.read: The tail risk of an October hike has eased, but a December hike remains the market's base case; the site's real yield is up 10bp over 20 days, and high rates keep capping valuation expansion. Macro backdrop, not a framework condition.

news.title: 24-hour liquidations across the market about $315M, 66% of them longs; Glassnode notes the loss-taking waves seen at the previous three local lows have reappeared, which could point to a floor just above $80K if the pattern holds
news.read: Liquidations were modest but long-heavy, consistent with the site's weighted funding falling from 9.81% to 3.80%: the leverage chased in a day earlier was flushed. The Glassnode floor is second-hand and an inference; the site's STH-SOPR of 1.0006 is still above 1 and the last two loss-taking lows show easing pressure. Reading only, not a buy signal.

news.title: Strive's holdings rose to 35,595 BTC, the fourth-largest public treasury, after purchases announced on 10/13–10/14; it upsized its SATS preferred offering to about $630M, expected to close 10/20; TD Cowen raised its target from $44 to $56
news.read: Some treasury companies are still accelerating buys while Strategy is under pressure, but the size is small next to a week of ETF outflows; the site's 1K–10K cohort at +11.8K BTC over 7 days may partly reflect such buying (addresses are not entities). It does not change the cycle call.

news.title: The Nasdaq closed Friday down 2.14% at 26,140.03 and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 3.83%, its worst week since April; the 10-year yield edged lower around 5.1%
news.read: Listed last edition; it carries into the weekend as backdrop. With a 0.668 BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation, weak tech is still a source of pressure, yet BTC has held above 80.6K for the two days since and has proven relatively resilient. Short-term risk appetite; it touches no framework condition.
